front: What is ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) in one sentence?
back: Regenerate static pages on a timer or on-demand without full site rebuild — Next.js stale-while-revalidate for CDN-backed pages.

front: Explain the mental model of ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) (how the system thinks).
back: At build time, page is static HTML. After deploy, first request (or revalidate interval) can trigger background regeneration. Users get stale page immediately while fresh version builds — then CDN serves new static file. Distinct from SSR (every request) and pure SSG (rebuild all).

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration)?
back: Request → CDN static (stale OK) → optional background regen → update CDN cache

back: Request → CDN static (stale OK) → optional background regen → update CDN cache

front: Symptom: Content never updates — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: revalidate set? · Fix: Add interval or on-demand hook

front: Symptom: Users see old data long — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: CDN TTL > revalidate · Fix: Align edge cache; purge CDN

front: Symptom: Build OK, prod stale — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Hosting ISR support · Fix: Vercel/Netlify plugin; not plain static export

front: Symptom: 401 on revalidate — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Secret mismatch · Fix: Match header + env

front: Symptom: Thundering herd regen — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Traffic spike on stale · Fix: Increase revalidate; use on-demand only

front: Gotcha with ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration): what silently fails?
back: output: 'export' disables ISR — pure static export has no server to revalidate. Stale content is a feature — document SLA ("up to 60s old") for editors. Personalized pages — don't ISR user-specific data; use SSR or client fetch.

front: When should you NOT use ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration)?
back: Don't ISR real-time dashboards (stock tickers, live scores) — use SSR/WebSocket. Don't ISR pages that must be legally exact at every view (some pricing) without short revalidate + purge.

front: What is Next.js navigation in one sentence?
back: Client-side routing in the App/Pages router — when to use Link, router, or a real new tab.

front: Explain the mental model of Next.js navigation (how the system thinks).
back: Next.js intercepts in-app navigation to avoid full page reloads. App Router uses next/navigation (useRouter, redirect, Link). Pages Router uses next/router. Opening a new browser tab/window is not SPA navigation — use <a target="_blank"> or window.open, not router.push.

front: Which standard commands / workflow do you use for Next.js navigation?
back: Same tab in-app → <Link href="..."> or router.push('/path') → New tab → <a href="..." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"> → Full reload → window.location.href = '...' (rare)

front: Given a broken Next.js navigation setup, what is your first validation command?
back: Same tab in-app → <Link href="..."> or router.push('/path')

front: Symptom: router.push doesn't open tab — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: API design · Fix: Use <a target="_blank">

front: Symptom: State lost on navigate — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Full remount · Fix: Lift state to URL/searchParams or store

front: Symptom: Back button weird — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Shallow routing misuse · Fix: App Router: use router.replace intentionally

front: Symptom: 404 on client nav — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Missing route file · Fix: Check app/ segment or pages/ file

front: Symptom: Scroll jumps — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Default scroll restore · Fix: scroll={false} on Link if needed

front: Gotcha with Next.js navigation: what silently fails?
back: router.push after async — component may unmount; check mounted or use transition API. External URLs in Link — must use plain <a>. Middleware redirect loops — login ↔ home; test cookie/session in middleware.

front: When should you NOT use Next.js navigation?
back: Don't router.push for file downloads — use <a download> or signed URL. Don't client-nav to logout that must clear httpOnly cookies — use server route/form POST.
